summary: Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (2006–2015) under Dan Arnold. His posts include Junior Fellow at the Max Planck Institute and Assistant Professor at Yale University (2022).

Sonam Kinga works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Sherubtse College (~1994–1998) and earned a PhD from Kyoto University (2007–2010). He was a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies (~1999–2007) and an AIAS fellow (2026).

Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Tasmania (1999–2002), where he was mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, becoming Senior Philosophy Lecturer there in 2003.

Sonam Tsering works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gray Tuttle as doctoral supervisor, among other teachers. As attested in 2026, he serves as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. As attested in 2026, she holds appointments as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Songeun Choe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonika Gupta specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1993–1997) and became a professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras in 2025.

Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA (1962–1966) and PhD (1970–1979) at the University of British Columbia, where she completed her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida.

Sonja Glauch specializes in linguistics. She completed her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she became Akademische Oberrätin in 2007, later holding visiting professorships at the University of Vienna (2008) and University of Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu. Her posts include teaching at Swarthmore College (2003–2004) and an appointment at USC (attested 2010).

Soonil Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1998–2003). In 2004, he became a professor at Dongguk University.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Pemaratana studied under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore at the National University of Singapore and is attested as a visiting professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, University of Copenhagen, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held posts as fellow (1860–1864) and lektor (1866) at the University of Oslo.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Nishioka is attested as a professor at Shitennoji University in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. After studying at Waseda University, he earned a master's and doctorate from Koyasan University, where he served as a researcher (attested 2015, 2026), and lectured at Sonoda Women's University.

Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor and dean (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soumyajit Sen is an Indologist who studied at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira and completed a Ph.D. at Jadavpur University (2016–2022). He taught at Sammilani Mahavidyalaya (2015–2016) before becoming Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.

Soyen Shaku (1860–1919) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University and under Kōsen Imakita. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
Spiridon Dmitrievič Èl’manovič (born 1844) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1865 to 1869 and served as director of Kholm Gymnasium in 1896.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Delhi and completed a PhD at Rice University (~2011–2016). Her appointments include instructional assistant professor at the University of Houston (2023).
